predecessors.name: Sui dynasty
predecessors.text: 'Zhejiang and southern Jiangsu, including Jiangnan' (Shen Faxing page infobox), capital Piling (modern Changzhou)

successors.name: Li Zitong's Wu
successors.text: 'Zhejiang and southern Jiangsu, including Jiangnan' (Shen Faxing page infobox), capital Piling (modern Changzhou)

ledger.x: 618: Shen Faxing, Sui governor of Wuxing Commandery, rises after Emperor Yang's death: he 'gathered the troops of the region (more than 60,000 men)' and 'occupied more than 10 commanderies', Piling among them.
Fall 619: Shen Faxing proclaims himself King of Liang and sets his capital at Piling.

wars.name: Li Zitong's conquest of Shen Faxing
wars.outcome: Li took Jingkou and Piling and the Liang territory; Shen died in 620.

certainty.note: A one-year rebel kingdom with no boundary on the page.
